name: eg
desc: Expert Guide. Norton Guide Reader For GNU/Linux
why: Reads Norton Guide hypertext help files on Linux, a forgotten DOS-era format with a genuinely strange lineage.

brief.what_it_is: Expert Guide (eg) is a terminal reader for Norton Guide hypertext help databases, the compiled help format used by Norton Guide and Expert Help. You give it a Norton Guide file and it lets you browse and navigate the content in a text-mode interface. The README says it is developed on and for GNU/Linux, can also run on macOS, and should be able to compile under DOS with DJGPP. It uses the S-Lang library for terminal display. The README does not describe the interface in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's site frames the wider project as keeping access to information in Norton Guide database files alive, since many of these help files date from the 1990s. The README says anyone who has used Norton Guide or Expert Help should find eg familiar.

commands_seen.context: Builds eg from source. The README says you need the slang library installed first.
Installs the built eg. The README says to check the settings at the top of the Makefile before building or installing.

brief.install_notes: You need the S-Lang library installed before building; the README points to jedsoft.org/slang for it. Build with make, then make install. Review the settings at the top of the Makefile first, since they control the build and install. The README also says it is installable via Homebrew, which is how this catalogue entry was reached. No accounts or runtimes beyond a C toolchain and slang are mentioned. A man page is included, but the README does not give its name.
brief.standout: It is a 1990s-era format reader with a real lineage: the davep.org page says Expert Guide began as an OS/2 text-mode Norton Guide reader, was rewritten for GNU/Linux, and has since been reworked for macOS. The same author maintains a family of related tools, including a Python library (ngdb.py), an HTML converter (ng2web), an Emacs package (eg.el), and a terminal reader called AgiNG.
brief.status: Unknown from the README alone. The README has no release date or changelog entry, and only one dated note (macOS support as of December 2015). It points readers to Changes, BUGS and TODO files and says the latest version lives at davep.org/norton-guides. The davep.org page calls the OS/2 version no longer supported, but does not say that about eg itself. The author's note that the project is 'developed on and for Linux' suggests it is maintained, but I did not see a recent commit or release date.
brief.caveats: The README says documentation is 'a little thin on the ground at the moment' and that a user document is still to be written; a man page covers the basics. Build and install depend on the slang library and the Makefile settings. Platform claims are loose: macOS is mentioned only in a footnote, and DOS/DJGPP compilation is described as possible rather than confirmed. Users are told to read the Changes, BUGS and TODO files. The davep.org page calls the author's w3ng tool deprecated, but that does not apply to eg. The project has no stated license in the README.
quotes: Documentation is a little thin on the ground at the moment.
anyone who has ever used Norton Guide or Expert Help should get to grips with Expert Guide with few problems.
eg is developed on and for Linux.

entry.title: eg (Expert Guide)
entry.tldr: A terminal reader for Norton Guide, the compiled hypertext help format from 1990s DOS programming tools, so old help files can be read on Linux.
entry.deeper_look:
Norton Guide was a hypertext help format from the DOS era. Programmers kept these compiled databases open while writing code, and they carried reference material for languages, libraries and tools. eg opens one of these files and lets you browse it in a text-mode interface drawn with the S-Lang library.

The author's site describes the wider project as keeping access to the information in these files alive, since many of them date from the 1990s. The README says anyone who has used Norton Guide or Expert Help should find eg familiar. It does not describe the interface in detail.

eg has a long lineage. According to the author's page, it began as an OS/2 text-mode Norton Guide reader, was rewritten for GNU/Linux, and was later reworked for macOS. The same author maintains related tools: a Python library (ngdb.py), an HTML converter (ng2web), an Emacs package (eg.el) and another terminal reader called AgiNG. Together they make a way into a small, nearly forgotten corner of software documentation history.

You need a Norton Guide file to read. The brief does not say where to find them, but the author's Norton Guides page is the place to start.
entry.install:
brew install eg
# Building from source instead: install S-Lang first, check the settings at the top of the Makefile, then run make and make install.
# You also need a Norton Guide file to open.

Installs the built eg. Check the Makefile settings first.

entry.whats_unique: It is a working reader for a 1990s help format, descended from an OS/2 tool, with a family of sibling tools for converting and reading the same files.
entry.caveats: Documentation is, in the README's words, "a little thin on the ground at the moment", and the brief could not confirm a recent release date.
